chapter.v:
Dead flies
can make perfumed oil smell bad. Likewise a little foolishness outweighs great wisdom and honor.

The mind
of the wise person chooses the right side, but the mind of the fool goes left!

Just the
way that fools walk down the road shows they have no sense, making clear to everyone their stupidity.

If your
superior gets angry with you, don't give up and leave. If you stay calm even bad mistakes can be resolved.

I also
realized there's another evil here on earth: rulers make a big mistake

when they
put fools in high positions, while those who are richly qualified are put in low positions.

I've seen
slaves riding on horseback, while princes walk on the ground like slaves.

If you
dig a pit, you could fall in. If you knock down a wall, you could be bitten by a snake.

If you
quarry stone, you could be injured. If you split logs, you could be hurt.

If your
ax is blunt and you don't sharpen it, you have to use a lot more force. Conclusion: being wise brings good results.

If the
snake bites the snake charmer before it's charmed, there's no benefit to the snake charmer!

Wise words
are beneficial, but fools destroy themselves by what they say.

Fools begin
by saying foolish things, and end up talking evil nonsense.

Fools talk
on and on, however no one knows what's going to happen, so who can say what the future holds?

Work makes
fools so worn out they can't achieve anything.

You're in
trouble if the king of your country is young, and if your leaders are busy feasting from early morning.

You're fortunate
if your king comes from a noble family, and your leaders feast at the proper time to give themselves energy, and not to get drunk.

Lazy people
let their roofs collapse; idle people don't repair their leaky houses.

A good
meal brings pleasure; wine makes life pleasant; money provides for all needs.

Don't talk
badly about the king, not even in your thoughts. Don't talk badly about leaders, even in the privacy of your bedroom. A bird may hear what you say and fly away to tell them.
